regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the quality check is IIP at 8.0% YoY with capital goods accelerating to 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity — these are not statistical artefacts. But core sector at 4.8% YoY, slipping from 5.0%, is the dissenting voice: infrastructure-linked output is softening even as manufacturing investment accelerates. The divergence suggests the investment upcycle is private-sector-led and concentrated in select industries, not yet broad-based enough to survive a credit tightening.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is 54 bps above RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY, and the composition is punishing: food at 7.74% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY are doing the heavy lifting, while core CPI sits at 3.9% YoY — the 28th percentile. The inversion: a central bank that focuses on core to justify a pause is ignoring that fuel inflation at the 95th percentile feeds into transport costs, which feed into food prices with a one-quarter lag. The second-order effect is that the food spike is not yet over.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY is a 160 bps divergence that has widened for two consecutive months — and the CD ratio at 81%, though easing from 82.2%, sits at the 73rd percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held, the RBI eventually moved on risk weights for unsecured lending. Services credit at 24.3% YoY — the fastest-growing segment — and NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY rising for two consecutive months are the pressure points: if deposit mobilisation stalls, the funding cost for NBFCs rises first.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed in real time: CPI has risen 71 bps since the last meeting while the policy rate has not moved. With RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY already above the 4% target midpoint, the pause is increasingly a choice to tolerate negative real rates rather than a signal of imminent easing. For housing, a 7.5% p.a. average home loan rate against 5.54% CPI is a real borrowing cost of roughly 200 bps — not restrictive enough to cool credit, not loose enough to accelerate it.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, rising from 16.1%, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — the 74th percentile and above the 75% threshold that historically triggers private capex commitments — together make the investment upcycle case. Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY, up sharply from 8.7%, is the commercial vehicle proxy: logistics operators are borrowing to expand fleet, which is a leading indicator of goods-economy confidence. The risk is that credit tightening — whether via RBI macro-prudential action or deposit-driven funding stress — arrives before the capex cycle completes its self-reinforcing loop.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a record, but the composition matters: passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are decelerating (down from 16% and 26.1% in prior months), while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY have bounced sharply. This is the classic dual-economy split — mass-market rural mobility recovering while urban discretionary (PV sales) softens. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is the tax on this recovery: every rupee spent at the pump is a rupee not spent at the mall, and e-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY — the 15th percentile — confirms that digital consumption is not picking up the slack.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now rising 2 in a row. Services credit at 24.3% YoY — highest growth segment, up from 10.3% YoY.","implication":"The deposit surge masks structural stress: banks are chasing credit growth faster than retail deposits can sustain. NBFCs are compensating with wholesale funding (corp bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month, though signal unknown). Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from PSU peers. Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their funding costs will spike if RBI tightens. Expect RBI to signal deposit-focused policy in next review, not rate cuts.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level. However, the 160 bps credit-deposit gap at this stage of the cycle has preceded NBFC stress and RBI tightening in 2018–19.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Capital Goods","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY, now at 52nd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 74th percentile — in the sweet spot for capex acceleration. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5%), but credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and credit to agriculture at 17.2% YoY (both rising 2 in a row) signal broad-based investment. Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (up from 8.7% YoY) — commercial vehicle proxy for logistics capex.","implication":"Capex is no longer a manufacturing story; it's spreading into services (credit to services +24.3% YoY) and agriculture. Overweight capital goods, cement, and logistics plays. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) are net buyers at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile), suggesting domestic money is rotating into capex beneficiaries. Avoid defensive sectors; the cycle is broadening. Watch for order book commentary in Q4 earnings — if order books are >12 months, capex will sustain into FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is historically the inflection point for capex acceleration. The last time it was here (2021–22), capex growth sustained for 18+ months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest), rising 3 in a row (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490), at 93rd percentile. SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (down from 10.45 mn, but signal mild-negative due to account churn). SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (up from ₹16.64 lakh cr), at 89th percentile. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (up from ₹29,329 cr / month), at 80th percentile. BUT: SIP YoY growth at 10.7% (down from 15% YoY) — growth is decelerating even as absolute inflows accelerate.","implication":"SIP inflows are at record highs, but the deceleration in YoY growth (15%→10.7%) combined with rising AUM per account signals a shift: affluent money is entering via SIPs, not mass retail. Average ticket size is rising. This is late-cycle behaviour — retail is chasing returns, not building discipline. DIIs are net buyers (₹51,829 cr / month), but FIIs are net sellers (₹-49,935 cr / month). Overweight large-cap, quality dividend payers; avoid small-cap momentum plays. Expect SIP growth to plateau or reverse if equity markets correct >10%.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile have preceded market corrections in 2018 and 2020. The combination of record inflows + decelerating growth is a classic late-cycle signal.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort Zone","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY, at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at $109.36 / bbl (up from $105.7 / bbl over recent months), at 75th percentile. WTI at $98.41 / bbl, at 81st percentile. Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83% YoY), driven by food (7.74% YoY, up from 5.97% YoY) and fuel. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY — already above the 4% target midpoint.","implication":"Fuel inflation is the tail risk to RBI's pause. If Brent stays >$110 / bbl, headline CPI will remain sticky above 5.5%, forcing RBI to signal hawkishness or risk credibility loss. India's oil import bill will spike; CAD will widen. Hedge long INR positions; expect depreciation pressure if oil stays elevated. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) for the near term, but avoid refiners (margin compression). Underweight consumer discretionary; margin pressure will be severe. Watch for RBI's next inflation forecast — if it revises up, rate cuts are off the table for 2026.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has only been exceeded during 2008 and 2022 oil shocks. This level has historically forced RBI into tightening cycles.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry; DXY Stable","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1% p.a.), at 100th percentile — highest in the dataset, rising 2 in a row. US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.15% (up from 5.09%), at 93rd percentile. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63%), at 68th percentile. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25%), rising 2 in a row. DXY at 101.792, flat, at 54th percentile. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (up from 56), at 91st percentile — US growth is strong.","implication":"BOJ tightening is the wild card. Carry trades funded in JPY are unwinding; this will create volatility in EM currencies and equities. DXY is stable (not spiking), which is good for INR, but if BOJ continues hiking, JPY strength will force global deleveraging. US growth remains robust (PMI 58.4, GDP 2.2% SAAR), so Fed is unlikely to cut aggressively. Expect 2–3 more Fed hikes before cuts resume. Overweight USD-denominated assets; underweight EM equities exposed to carry unwind. India is relatively insulated (FII outflows already priced in at ₹-49,935 cr / month), but watch for sudden spikes in US VIX (currently 17.31, at 11th percentile — complacent).","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"US 10Y yield at 93rd percentile combined with BOJ at 100th percentile is a rare regime — last seen in 2018 before the Fed pivot. This typically precedes EM stress.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens as Oil Imports Surge; RBI Intervenes","data_text":"INR at 94.34 ₹ / USD (down from 94.99, i.e., weakening), at 87th percentile — near multi-year lows. Recent trend: 96.15→95.24→96.15→97.09→96.15→95.24 (volatile, but trending weaker). Brent at $109.36 / bbl (75th percentile) and fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) imply India's oil import bill is rising sharply. FII equity outflows at ₹-49,935 cr / month (17th percentile — weak) are adding depreciation pressure. DXY at 101.792 (54th percentile) is stable, so INR weakness is India-specific, not a broad EM story.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to defend INR (CD ratio falling 2 in a row suggests RBI is using reserves). If oil stays >$110 / bbl, INR will test 96–97 levels. Importers should hedge; exporters should delay hedging. FII outflows will persist if equity returns disappoint — watch for any sign of FII reversal (currently ₹-49,935 cr / month). CAD will widen; expect RBI to signal INR stability in next policy review. Avoid long INR positions; overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto components) for natural hedges.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile (near historical weakness) combined with oil at 75th percentile has preceded RBI tightening and import compression in 2018–19.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 5.3 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 3.9 mn sq ft / quarter, but signal is strong-negative (score: -100) because the 10-year percentile is 0% lo — this is a structural break. Recent trend: 21→13.2→4.02→13.2→14.1→4 (volatile, but collapsing). Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (up from 13.74%), at 41st percentile. Nifty IT index is flat (no major weakness). BUT: Rent in Bengaluru at ₹102 / sqft / month (up from ₹94.5), at 58th percentile — rents are rising despite absorption collapse. This is the tell: GCCs (Global Capability Centers) are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses; traditional IT services are shrinking footprints.","implication":"The office market is bifurcating. GCCs are the buyer (consolidating, paying premium rents for trophy assets), while traditional IT services are shedding space. This means: (1) Overweight commercial RE REITs with GCC-heavy portfolios (Embassy, Mindspace) — they'll capture the consolidation premium. (2) Underweight mid-tier IT services with high real estate costs; they're losing the space arbitrage. (3) Watch for Q4 earnings commentary on real estate costs — if IT services report lower occupancy costs, it's a margin positive, not a demand negative. (4) The absorption collapse is NOT a recession signal; it's a structural shift in how tech companies organize work.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile (lowest in 10 years) would normally signal a recession. However, rising rents in Bengaluru (58th percentile) and stable Nifty IT (flat) suggest this is a supply-side consolidation, not demand destruction. This divergence has not been seen before — it's a genuine structural shift.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Fuel Bill Is Eating the Dividend

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY with PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) — both manufacturing and services expanding.
  • IIP Capital Goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) confirm the investment cycle is real, not budgeted.
  • But fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) and food at 7.74% YoY push headline CPI to 5.54% YoY — 54 bps above RBI's own forecast.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural recovery; passenger vehicle sales decelerating to 7.9% YoY signal urban softness — the economy is not moving uniformly.

The tension: Growth metrics point to expansion; inflation metrics point to a tax on that expansion. Fuel at the 95th percentile compresses real incomes faster than 7.8% nominal GDP can replenish them.

Bottom line: Watch core CPI — at 3.9% YoY it is the RBI's alibi for a pause; if it crosses 4.5% YoY, the pause becomes untenable.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Acceleration Meets BOJ Tightening — EM Caught Between

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile), rising for two consecutive months — US growth is not slowing.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 5.15% yield (93rd percentile) with Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. — the bond market is tightening independently of the Fed.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in the dataset) — yen carry unwind pressure is structural, not episodic.
  • Nikkei at 64,075 (100th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,122 (100th percentile) are both retreating from peaks — DM equity at record valuations while real rates rise.

The tension: Strong US growth justifies higher-for-longer rates, which compresses EM risk appetite. BOJ tightening simultaneously unwinds the carry trade that funded EM inflows — India faces both pressures at once.

Bottom line: If US 10Y Treasury breaches 5.25% yield, FII outflows from India — already at ₹49,935 cr net / month — accelerate; hedge INR exposure.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds; Smart Money Signals Caution

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive months — retail participation is structurally sticky.
  • Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr net / month (80th percentile), up from ₹29,329 cr net / month — DII absorption is absorbing FII selling.
  • But FII equity net at ₹-49,935 cr net / month (17th percentile) — foreign selling is at its most intense since the pre-Budget scramble.
  • NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile, 10-year low) — asset managers are not launching new products, which is the institutional signal that valuations are stretched.

The tension: Retail SIPs are providing a mechanical floor under equities; institutional fund managers are simultaneously refusing to launch new vehicles at current prices. The floor is real but not unlimited.

Bottom line: DII net absorption at ₹51,829 cr net / month is the circuit breaker — if SIP growth decelerates below 8% YoY, the FII-DII offset collapses.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Mispriced as GCC Consolidation Rewrites Office Demand

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 10 pp vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; Hyderabad (sales +15% YoY) and Bengaluru (sales +12% YoY) are the primary destinations.
  • Premium supply (₹80 lakh – ₹1.5 cr) commands 31% of launches — the largest single band — while affordable (<₹40 lakh) at 14% of launches is undersupplied relative to 16% of sales demand.
  • Office absorption at 5.3 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile — structural break) while Bengaluru rents rise to ₹102/sqft/mo — GCCs (41% of occupier mix) consolidating into fewer campuses, not exiting.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior levels — the market is pricing IT-services vacancy, not GCC consolidation.

The tension: Rising rents and GCC dominance (41% of leasing) signal structural demand; collapsing absorption and REIT unit prices signal the market is reading the wrong signal — IT services shrinkage, not GCC growth.

Bottom line: Embassy and Mindspace REITs are mispriced if GCC consolidation sustains — watch Hyderabad vacancy (currently 24%) as the leading indicator of whether consolidation is absorbing or abandoning space.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Pressure Points, One Trigger

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $109.36/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill; CAD widens ~40 bps; INR depreciates further from its current 87th-percentile 94.34 ₹.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — yen carry unwind is the underpriced tail; FII outflows at ₹-49,935 cr net / month could double if US 10Y Treasury holds above 5.15% yield.
  • CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits (73rd percentile) with credit growing at 19.4% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights becomes probable within two quarters.
  • But core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile) is the RBI's cover for inaction — if food inflation feeds into core via transport costs, the pause ends and rate-sensitive sectors (housing, autos, NBFCs) reprice simultaneously.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — an oil spike widens CAD, weakens INR, imports inflation into core CPI, forces RBI off its pause, and tightens credit conditions precisely when the capex cycle needs funding.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a sustained print above $112/bbl triggers the CAD-INR-inflation chain and makes the RBI's extended pause politically and arithmetically untenable.

"}
